picks.style: sanskrit cosmogonic chant, tanpura drone and deep frame drum, resonant male voice, slow, vast, ritual
picks.why: The Boar lifting the drowned earth, his whole body read as a sacrifice — tusks the sacrificial post, grunt the Sāma chant.

picks.style: namavali litany, harmonium and hand cymbals, call-and-response male voices, steady, hypnotic, devotional
picks.why: A litany of names of the god — already built to be sung antiphonally: O you without beginning, middle, or end.

picks.style: ascetic chant, single drone and finger cymbals, austere male voice, sparse, unhurried, resolute
picks.why: The tapas couplets: austerity as root, middle and end of the world, and nothing insurmountable to it.

picks.style: spenserian pastoral, lute and recorder, warm tenor, gentle, unhurried, sunlit
picks.why: The hermitage stanza — vine-wound cottage, hundred flowers, a brook that lulls to sleep profound.

picks.style: gothic ballad, viol and low drone, dark baritone, slow, eerie, brooding
picks.why: The turf cottage under the yew, the owl's dirge, and the old miser bound in a golden fillet.

picks.style: archaic ballad, harp and fiddle, plain male voice, measured, wry, elegiac
picks.why: Troy town is now a grass-grown field — the sun itself shall lose its light, and mortal flesh is frail.

picks.style: homeric hymn, phorminx lyre and light drum, clear male voice, stately, invocatory, flowing
picks.why: The proem: the goddess who subdues gods, mortals, birds of the air and everything the sea rears.

picks.style: greek lament, single lyre and low drone, ageing male voice, slow, hollow, haunted
picks.why: Tithonus granted deathlessness without youth — shut in a room, babbling endlessly, unable to lift a limb.

picks.style: pastoral hymn, syrinx and soft strings, mid-range voice, gentle, mysterious, unhurried
picks.why: The mountain nymphs whose pines and oaks are born with them and wither when their lives run out.

picks.style: english hymn, chamber organ and voices, congregational tenor, steady, majestic, common meter
picks.why: Great God, indulge a mortal tongue — and the line that has outlived it: thou sit'st on no precarious throne.

picks.style: sapphic doom hymn, low drums and drone, massed unison voices, driving, terrifying, relentless
picks.why: The Day of Judgment in sapphics — graves opening, the living worm, hopeless immortals screaming.

picks.style: children's hymn, acoustic guitar and recorder, sweet clear voice, simple, gentle, lilting
picks.why: The rose that fades in a day but keeps its perfume — Watts's plainest and best-turned emblem.

picks.style: hellenistic bucolic dirge, syrinx and lyre, plaintive male voice, slow, refrain-driven, mourning
picks.why: The opening dirge with its refrain — roses flushing crimson, the hyacinth told to speak its letters.

picks.style: pastoral lament, low strings and reed pipe, grave voice, slow, resigned, dark
picks.why: Mallows and parsley come back each year; we, once dead, sleep an endless unwakeable sleep.

picks.style: bucolic elegy, solo panpipes and soft drum, tender male voice, unhurried, aching
picks.why: Who is bold enough to set his mouth to your reeds — even Pan would fear to come off second.

picks.style: greek symposium song, lyre and aulos, wry male voice, moderate, conversational, sardonic
picks.why: Hesiod's marriage arithmetic followed by the hundred names of Cypris — she's hell on earth, continued violence.

picks.style: epigraphic chant, single lyre and sea-drone, sparse male voice, slow, weathered, monumental
picks.why: The inscription on the stone ship: me, a ship of stone, Agamemnon set up here.
